newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russian refinery project back on track - Mitsui.
newsitem.headline: Russian refinery project back on track - Mitsui.

text.p: Mitsui & Co Ltd said on Monday its 28-billion-yen ($248.2 million) Russian oil refinery project near Moscow, dormant since 1995, should be back on track soon.

The Yaroslavl refinery, some 300 km (190 miles) northeast of Moscow, awarded a contract to a Japanese-German consortium comprised of Mitsui and Thyssen Rheinstahl Technik GmbH in 1995. The contract covered construction of a catalytic reformer with an annual output capacity of two million tonnes.
The deal sputtered when the Russian refiner failed to raise an initial down payment, but Mitsui now says the project may proceed as planned.
"We have an impression that the Russian side is now set to pay the rest of the down payment," said a Mitsui spokesman, without elaborating on the source of the assurance.

The comment coincided with a Russian delegation visit to Tokyo headed by Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov. Nemtsov, who also serves as Russian Fuel and Energy Minister, was courting new Japanese investment in the Russian economy.
Eighty-five percent, or 23.8 billion yen, of the Yaroslavl project was to be financed with a loan from the Export-Import Bank of Japan, with the rest shouldered by the refinery.
The refinery paid only five percent, or 1.4 billion yen, of the requisite 15 percent downpayment, the Mitsui spokesman said.

The Export-Import Bank of Japan is to extend the remainder of the cost only after the refinery has paid its down payment in full and opened a letter of credit at a Russian bank, an Ex-Im bank spokesman said.
The Russian refinery is believed to be in the process of opening the letter of credit, the Mitsui spokesman said.
